key: A grandmother teaching a five-year-old to make rotis
name: ch27_grandmother_roti_lesson
alt: A grandmother sits on a low stool by the stove with her small grandchild, praising the puffed side of a lopsided first roti while a row of rotis grows rounder towards the tenth.
scene: A warm, wide view of a small Indian home kitchen in late afternoon. On the LEFT, a grandmother in her late sixties (cream cotton sari with a plum border, grey hair in a bun, round spectacles) sits on a low wooden stool beside a two-burner stove with a black iron tawa, smiling broadly and pointing with one finger at a roti in her other hand. Beside her, a five-year-old child (yellow frock, two short pigtails, flour on her cheeks) kneels at a round wooden board with a small rolling pin, grabbing the next ball of dough eagerly, face proud. A steel plate of dough balls and a dusting bowl of flour sit nearby. The grandmother's speech bubble shows the lopsided roti with a small puffed bump circled and a green tick, nothing about the burnt bit. Along the bottom RIGHT, a long steel plate holds a row of rotis laid left to right: the first shaped like a lumpy map, half pale and half with brown burn spots; each next roti slightly rounder and more evenly browned; the last one almost a perfect circle. A thin dashed arrow runs under the row from first to last. Soft golden window light, gentle and cheerful. Labels: "FIRST" under the lumpy first roti, "TENTH" under the round last roti.

key: A girl in a small town sings bhajans
name: ch27_mother_hears_high_note
alt: Split picture: at school a music teacher dismisses a girl's thin voice in front of the class; at home that evening her mother listens to her practise and notices the high note did not crack.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same girl of about twelve (green school pinafore over white shirt, long plait) in both halves. LEFT panel: a plain small-town classroom with a blackboard and wooden benches; a stern male music teacher (fifties, brown kurta, spectacles) stands beside a harmonium, pointing away towards a drawing chart on the wall as if sending her off; the girl stands with shoulders hunched and eyes down while three classmates on the bench turn to stare. A red cross badge floats near the girl. RIGHT panel: evening in a one-room home with a single bulb and a small brass lamp; the girl sings with her chin up and her hands folded, a musical note rising cleanly from her mouth along a smooth curve; her mother (forties, faded blue cotton sari, tired but glowing face) sits on a mat folding laundry, looking up proudly, one hand raised as if to say well done. Pinned on the wall behind them is a small paper flyer with a music note for a weekend class, and beside it a sari price tag with a line crossed through it, showing what the mother gave up. Labels: "TOO THIN" at the top of the left panel, "NO CRACK TODAY" at the top of the right panel.

key: A first-year engineering student in a hostel
name: ch27_editor_please_send_more
alt: A hostel student walks the campus at midnight reading a one-line note from an editor in his printed Sunday story, ten rejected envelopes left behind in his room.
scene: A night scene on an Indian engineering college campus, kept bright and readable. On the LEFT, cut away through a hostel room window, a narrow steel bed with a thin mattress lifted at one corner shows a hidden notebook beneath it; on the desk beside it sits a small stack of ten brown envelopes, each stamped with a small red cross, some torn open. In the CENTRE and RIGHT, on a lamp-lit path between the hostel block and a large neem tree, a lanky first-year student (about eighteen, loose grey T-shirt, track pants, rubber slippers, messy hair) walks slowly, holding open a folded Sunday newspaper supplement with both hands, staring at it with a stunned, shy smile. An inset bubble zooms into the page: a small printed story column with a short handwritten note clipped beside it reading "Please send more". Small repeated eye-lines or a little loop arrow around the note show him rereading it again and again. A crescent moon and a few stars sit in the upper sky; the street lamp throws a warm pool of light around him. Mood: quiet, private joy. Labels: "10 REJECTED" above the envelope stack, "PRINTED" above the inset of the newspaper page.

key: A nineteen-year-old in Surat spends twelve hours
name: ch27_teacher_calls_back
alt: Split picture: a tired young man folds saris late at night in his uncle's shop and gets a call from his old maths teacher; two years later he teaches a weekend tuition batch at a blackboard.
scene: A split-panel picture divided by a thin vertical line, the same young man (nineteen, slim, plain white shirt, short hair) in both halves. LEFT panel: late night inside a narrow textile shop in Surat, shelves stacked high with folded saris in coral, teal and gold; he sits cross-legged on a white cotton floor mattress surrounded by piles of saris, shoulders slumped, holding up a phone whose screen shows a sad message bubble; a wall clock reads close to eleven. A dashed arrow runs from his phone across the divider line, ending in a ringing phone icon held by his old maths teacher, a kindly woman in her fifties (maroon salwar suit, spectacles, grey streak in her hair), drawn small at the top of the right panel inside a round inset bubble, smiling as she calls back. RIGHT panel: a bright weekend morning in a simple tuition room; the same young man now stands confidently at a green blackboard covered with a geometry figure and a short proof, chalk in hand, while four Class 8 students in school uniforms sit on benches with notebooks, two of them raising their hands. A small mortarboard cap and a book on the teacher's desk hint at his B.Ed studies. Labels: "12 HOURS" at the top of the left panel, "CLASS 8 BATCH" at the top of the right panel.

key: Two gardens in a housing colony
name: ch27_two_gardens_watering
alt: Split picture of two colony gardens: a grumbling man pulls weeds every evening among thin plants, while a woman waters tulsi, roses and curry leaf so thick that weeds get no light.
scene: A split-panel picture of two small front gardens side by side in an Indian housing colony, divided by a low brick wall drawn as a thin vertical line, evening light. LEFT panel: a middle-aged man (fifties, white vest, checked lungi, bald patch) squats in bare brown soil, frowning, yanking up a fistful of weeds with a small pile of pulled weeds beside him; around him many spiky green weeds are still sprouting, while a few wanted plants in the bed look thin, pale and droopy; a dry, unused watering can lies on its side; a small grumble cloud with a squiggle floats above his head. RIGHT panel: a woman in her forties (teal cotton sari, hair in a bun, small bindi) stands smiling with a green watering can, water streaming in arcs onto a lush bed: a tall tulsi plant in a square clay planter in the centre, a rose bush full of coral blooms, a dense curry leaf shrub; their thick canopy casts a dark shadow over the soil, where only one or two tiny weeds peek out, pale and starved. A small sack of compost sits by her feet. Soft golden evening sky over both gardens. Labels: "PULL WEEDS" at the top of the left panel, "FEED PLANTS" at the top of the right panel.

key: Evening homework in a Chennai flat
name: ch27_one_neat_line
alt: A mother at the dining table finds the one neat line in her son's messy homework and praises it; the next evening he shows her two neat lines before she asks.
scene: An evening scene in a small Chennai flat with a ceiling fan and a window showing a dusk sky. At a simple wooden dining table, a mother in her late thirties (mustard cotton sari, jasmine in her hair, reading glasses pushed up) leans over her son's open notebook, her finger resting under one line, her expression soft and pleased instead of angry. Her son (about eight, white school shirt with a loosened tie, short hair) sits beside her, pencil in hand, sitting up straighter, a small surprised smile starting. A crumpled eraser and a steel tumbler of milk are on the table. A large inset bubble zooms into the notebook page: several lines of wobbly, slanting, scrawled handwriting drawn as squiggles, and in the middle one line of clean, evenly spaced letters drawn as neat loops, highlighted with an amber glow and a small gold star beside it. On the RIGHT, a second smaller inset framed like a calendar page marked next day shows the boy proudly holding the notebook up towards his mother, now with two neat lines glowing. A faint grey cloud with a cross in the corner hints at the old shouting routine being left behind. Warm lamp light. Labels: "ONE NEAT LINE" above the big notebook inset, "NEXT DAY" above the small right inset.

key: A new waiter at a busy Udupi restaurant
name: ch27_waiter_feedback_book
alt: In a busy Udupi restaurant the owner shows a nervous new waiter a warm customer note in the feedback book, while the frowning head waiter looks on.
scene: A lively interior of a South Indian Udupi restaurant at lunchtime: steel tables, steel tumblers, banana-leaf plates with dosas, a cash counter with a small brass lamp in the background. In the CENTRE, the restaurant owner (sixties, white shirt, white veshti, holy ash stripe on forehead, spectacles) holds open a thick feedback book and points to a long handwritten entry, smiling warmly at the new waiter. The new waiter (early twenties, maroon uniform shirt, small notepad tucked in his pocket, thin moustache) stands with a tray under his arm, looking up from the book in surprise, shoulders lifting. An inset bubble zooms into the open book: many lines of handwriting drawn as squiggles, ending in a small heart and a smiling face. On the RIGHT, at a corner table, an elderly couple (grey-haired man in a half-sleeve shirt, woman in a green silk sari) sit finishing filter coffee in steel tumblers, nodding contentedly; a dotted line links them to the book. On the far LEFT, near the kitchen hatch, the head waiter (forties, stout, arms crossed) watches with a frown and a small question-mark badge above him. Busy, warm midday light. Labels: "FEEDBACK" above the inset of the book, "REAL PRAISE" near the owner and waiter at the top centre.

key: At a wedding, a hundred guests tell the cook
name: ch27_cook_specific_praise
alt: At a wedding, many guests mumble food was very nice on their way out, but one old uncle walks into the kitchen and praises the exact sourness of the bisi bele bath and the crisp boondi.
scene: A wide view split loosely in two by a kitchen doorway at a South Indian wedding hall at night. LEFT side: the exit of the dining hall with marigold garlands on the doorframe; a stream of four or five guests in silk saris and shirts walk out in a line, waving vaguely towards the kitchen; small pale grey speech bubbles float above them, each with only a tiny faded thumbs-up, overlapping and fading into each other. RIGHT side: inside a busy wedding kitchen with huge aluminium vessels on gas burners; the cook (fifties, sleeveless banian, towel on shoulder, sweat on forehead) stands by a big pot of bisi bele bath with a long ladle, turning towards an old uncle (seventies, white veshti, cream shirt, walking stick, spectacles) who has stepped into the kitchen and is speaking with one finger raised. The uncle's large white speech bubble holds three clear icons: a bowl of brown-orange bisi bele bath with a small tamarind pod, a bowl of white raita with round boondi dots, and a small clock showing ten o'clock. The cook's face lights up in a wide surprised smile, hand on heart. Warm yellow kitchen light, steam rising. Labels: "VERY NICE" in small type above the faded bubbles on the left, "SPECIFIC" above the uncle's big bubble on the right.

key: A cricket coach at a small-town academy
name: ch27_coach_spots_wrist
alt: At an evening cricket net, a coach points to a shy boy's wrist after a spinning delivery and asks him to do it again, as the boy realises he can bowl.
scene: An evening scene at the cricket nets of a small-town academy, green netting stretched on poles, a dusty run-up, a single floodlight just turning on against a pale dusk sky. In the CENTRE-LEFT, a shy twelve-year-old boy (white cricket clothes slightly too big, cap pushed back, thin arms) has just released the ball, his bowling arm high and his wrist flicked sideways; a dashed curving arrow traces the ball's path dipping and turning towards a single stump at the far end of the net, a small spin swirl drawn on the ball. On the RIGHT, standing just outside the net, the coach (forties, navy tracksuit, whistle on a cord, cap, short beard) leans in with one hand pointing at the boy's wrist and the other raised, saying something encouraging. A round inset bubble near the boy zooms in on his hand and wrist mid-flick with a small curved arrow showing the turn, glowing with an amber outline. In the background, a few other boys in whites carry kit bags towards the gate, not watching. Near the boy's feet lies a fielder's practice cone, hinting he thought he was only a fielder. Warm, encouraging mood. Labels: "WRIST" above the inset bubble, "DO IT AGAIN" above the coach.
